state.question: Why do instruments measuring ostensibly the same physical quantity (pendulum period and resonator frequency) show near-zero or negative cross-correlation at multiple time offsets, while individual instruments show no systematic drift or autocorrelation structure—suggesting either independent measurement error, calibration divergence between lab and observational setups, or genuine physical non-stationarity in the measurand itself?

hypotheses.label: Independent random measurement error in each channel
hypotheses.rationale: Cross-correlations between all instrument pairs are either insignificant (within chance), negative, or barely above chance at cherry-picked offsets. Within-instrument autocorrelations are uniformly weak. No instrument shows coherent drift or level change. Baselines are clean (104–52 distinct values across 48–110 trials; minimum spacings at instrumental precision). This pattern is exactly what one expects from four independent white-noise measurement channels.
